units.function: Managed/global update tests for mode/channel/version selection, source isolation, backup, side-by-side activation, service validation and binary rollback.
units.dependencyDirection: Uses real temporary install-store state with mocked package/source commands, backup and service restart callbacks.
units.keyDataModels: Install mode/manifest/history, npm channel/version, Git ref/SHA, payload/current link, backup and active-service restart result.
units.lifecycle: Resolve target, confirm downgrade/source execution, back up, stage/activate, restart/validate and flip back/restart old payload on failure.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 14/14. It strongly covers binary activation and restart rollback, but omits artifact authenticity, database migration rollback/compatibility, concurrent update races, crash consistency and accountable approval evidence.
units.designRationale: Make self-hosted updates recoverable while supporting channels, pinned refs and explicit downgrade/source consent.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs signed, evidence-backed cloud/local release trains with data migration compatibility and safe execution-node coordination.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the side-by-side tests, hostile registry isolation, backup gate, check exit code and two-stage restart-failure assertions. Add database forward/backward compatibility, backup restore, transaction ownership, signed artifact/SBOM and concurrent/crash matrices.
units.responsibilityConflict: The tests do not bind the requested update, source/dependency digests, backup, migration and restart results to an accountable operator and approval chain.

units.function: Tests for update-check kill switches and 24-hour registry caching.
units.dependencyDirection: Uses temporary config/cache files and an injected fetch response.
units.keyDataModels: Update configuration, checkedAt/latest cache and registry dist-tag response.
units.lifecycle: Disable or fetch once, cache and reuse the latest version during the throttle window.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 2/2. It omits malformed/future cache, link/mode safety, timeouts/failures, response bounds/version validation and privacy disclosure.
units.designRationale: Avoid a registry request on every CLI invocation while allowing operators to disable checks.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs profile-aware release notifications that respect enterprise egress policy and local/offline deployments.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT only after adding explicit egress policy, fail-closed invalid-config behavior, safe atomic cache, schema/time bounds, stable codes and managed-cloud/self-hosted defaults.
units.responsibilityConflict: A release notice is not authority to update; the test model contains no operator policy or approved maintenance window.

units.function: Managed installer for exact npm releases or full-SHA GitHub source builds, including staging, smoke check, current/manifest/shim activation and PATH setup.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI options and ambient registry/GitHub credentials drive network downloads and arbitrary package/source build scripts; results mutate the managed install store and shell configuration.
units.keyDataModels: Install request/channel, repo/ref/full SHA, release-package manifest, staged payload, InstallRecord/Manifest/current link/shim and PATH block.
units.lifecycle: Resolve source, optionally consent, download/install/build/package, smoke-check version, activate under lock, persist manifest/shim, prune and expose shim on PATH.
units.testAssessment: The previously audited install-command suite passed 16/16 and proves many filesystem/source safety properties, but the implementation still lacks artifact identity and a unified update transaction.
units.designRationale: Give users a reproducible managed binary layout with full-SHA source provenance, atomic payload selection and data-independent uninstall/update support.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS self-hosted/FDE delivery needs trusted, repeatable releases that cannot bypass data migration, service and approval controls.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY. Reuse selected helpers only after provenance review. A canonical release transaction must own install/update, signatures/digests/SBOM, sandboxed build, backup/migration, service health and rollback; install must not be an alternate upgrade path.
units.responsibilityConflict: Source consent is not bound to exact dependency/artifact digests, data migration or service changes. Existing managed installs can be switched without accountable update approval/evidence.

units.function: Update/check/downgrade/rollback orchestration for managed npm/Git installs and global npm installs.
units.dependencyDirection: Install metadata and executable-path heuristics select behavior; registry/GitHub resolution, database backup, install helpers, store locks and service restart implement the transaction.
units.keyDataModels: InstallMode, UpdateOptions/request, manifest/current/previous payloads, backup state, service health/version and restart intent/report.
units.lifecycle: Detect mode, resolve/check target, confirm risk, back up, stage/activate, restart/validate, automatically flip binaries back on failure or explicitly roll back.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests pass, but migration rollback, concurrency and inactive-service validation are missing production-critical dimensions.
units.designRationale: Provide safe-looking in-place updates with pre-update backup and rapid binary rollback.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS requires release orchestration across independent control/data/execution planes without corrupting customer data or responsibility continuity.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY for the orchestration; ADAPT small pure helpers/tests. Replace it with a durable release state machine that locks the full transaction, pins signed artifacts, records backup/schema compatibility, validates inactive profiles, coordinates nodes and restores or rolls forward data safely.
units.responsibilityConflict: Binary rollback can restart an older version after the failed new version migrated the database, without restoring the backup. The action, backup and resulting service state are not bound to accountable approval or immutable evidence.

units.function: Default-enabled, throttled npm registry version check with config/environment disable switches.
units.dependencyDirection: Reads product config/install channel/cache, performs a public-registry fetch and writes a user-level cache before printing human text.
units.keyDataModels: updates.checkEnabled, managed channel, checkedAt/latest cache, packageVersion and registry dist-tags.
units.lifecycle: Honor switches, reuse fresh cache, fetch selected tag, cache result and return a newer version when present.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests pass 2/2; adversarial filesystem/network/version/privacy cases are absent.
units.designRationale: Offer low-frequency update awareness with graceful offline failure.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS local enterprise deployments need explicit data-egress governance and offline-safe release observation.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the tiny cache concept behind an EgressPolicy/ReleaseMetadataPort. Invalid config should not silently enable network, and cache writes need trust/atomicity guards.
units.responsibilityConflict: Notification is informational and must never imply permission to install; maintenance ownership and approval remain separate.
